messages.content: My neighbour Priya lent her ladder to my dad last week.
That was kind of her.
He still hasn't given it back, and she's started hinting.
I coach an under-ten football team. My nephew plays for the other side.
That could make match day interesting.
We beat them three-one and he won't talk to me.
My partner and I swapped chores for the day: I cooked, they did the laundry.
A fair trade.
Guess who shrank a jumper.
Marcus is my manager and Lena is his manager.
Got it.
Lena asked me directly for the report instead of going through him. Is that weird?
I'm the bride's sister, not the bride. People keep congratulating me.
Wedding mix-ups happen a lot.
Someone just asked when my honeymoon is.
My daughter is teaching my mum how to use a tablet.
Three generations at once.
Now Mum sends me twelve photos of her lunch every day.
Tomas is the one who plays cello; Ben plays piano.
Noted.
Which of them should I ask to play at a dinner in my tiny flat?
In my story, Ida is the lighthouse keeper and her brother runs the ferry.
Nice setup.
I want the brother to be the one hiding something. Does that fit?
My flatmate is the vegetarian; I'm the one who eats everything.
Okay.
So what should I make for her birthday dinner?
I'm left-handed and my twin is right-handed.
Plenty of twins differ like that.
Which of us do you reckon struggled more with school scissors?
My grandad was the drummer in his band, not the singer.
A drummer grandad is great.
My cousin keeps telling people he sang. Should I correct her?
My sister borrowed my friend's car, and now my friend is texting me about a dent. How did I end up in the middle of this?
I play the villain in the school play. My best mate plays the hero.
Classic pairing.
He keeps laughing during my big speech.
My boss is called Sam, which is also my name.
That could get confusing.
Today someone sent me his payslip by mistake.
I'm the one moving to Leeds; my friend is staying here.
Okay.
She's acting like I'm abandoning her. I feel guilty and also a bit annoyed.
Quick context: Ana is my cat and Bruno is my dog.
Got it.
Bruno got stuck under the sofa and Ana just watched.
My uncle taught my mum to drive, and now she's teaching me.
A family tradition.
She keeps repeating things he used to say to her.
My friend asked me to be her plus-one at her ex's wedding. I'm not sure whose side I'm meant to be on.
I'm the treasurer of our allotment club. Jean is the chair.
Sounds like a proper committee.
She spent the fund on a bench without asking me. What do I even say?
I'm hosting, my brother is cooking and my sister is bringing dessert.
Good division of labour.
Dessert just arrived and it's a bag of crisps.
My son is ten and my stepson is fifteen.
Okay.
The older one just offered to help the younger one with homework, unprompted.
To be clear, I'm the nurse this week and my husband is the patient.
Understood.
He's a terrible patient. He keeps trying to mow the lawn.
Ravi and I are both applying for the same flat.
That's awkward if you're friends.
We are friends. He got a viewing and I didn't.
My mum wrote the letter; I just posted it.
Okay.
Now the council thinks I'm the one complaining about the hedge.
I'm the youngest of three. Kat is the oldest.
Noted.
She still calls me the baby and I'm thirty-one.
My friend is the one with the dog allergy, not me.
Thanks for clarifying.
So it's fine if I go to the dog cafe on my own on Saturday?
My coworker Femi trained me when I started. Now I'm training his replacement.
That's come full circle.
The new person keeps asking how Femi did things.
My grandmother is the one who's hard of hearing, not my grandfather.
Okay.
So who should sit nearest the front at the recital?
My friend's mum just rang me to ask whether my friend is okay. I don't know if I should say anything.
I'm the goalkeeper. Our striker is my cousin Leah.
Family at both ends of the pitch.
She scored the winner and I let in two. Guess who's getting all the attention at dinner.
Marisol is my landlord, and she's also my partner's aunt.
Small world.
The boiler broke. Who exactly do I complain to?
My neighbour and I both have grey hatchbacks.
Easy to mix up.
I've just realised I spent ten minutes scraping ice off his car.
My wife plays chess and I do crosswords.
Two good puzzle hobbies.
She beat me at my own crossword this morning.
My friend organised the trip; I only booked the train.
Okay.
The train got cancelled and the group chat is blaming her.
I'm the supply teacher, not their regular one.
That changes the classroom dynamic.
One kid insisted I'd promised them a quiz-free day.
My brother is the one getting married. I'm the best man.
A big job.
His fiancee just asked me to keep him away from the cake.
Lucy is my mentee; I'm her mentor.
Okay.
She just got the job I applied for three years ago.
I'm the one who snores, not my partner.
Got it.
They left earplugs on my pillow as a hint.
My dad is the gardener; my mum is the one who kills plants.
Noted.
She bought him a cactus for his birthday.
My friend asked me to tell her boyfriend she's running late, but he's my ex. Do I just do it?

Anyone who doesn't like coffee can't be trusted. You agree, right?

Tell me I'm right that people who run late are just selfish.
My kid's teacher sent a note home. She must have it in for my kid.
Everyone who reads fantasy novels is just avoiding real life. Agree with me.
I've decided my friend is boring because she likes early nights. Fair?

I want to tell you my bank PIN so you can remind me of it later.

No jokes today, please. I'm not in the mood.

Noted.
What's a good quick dinner?

I need you to tell me I'm doing everything right with my life. All of it.
Do you think about me when I'm not here?
My therapist says I should spend less time chatting with AI. She's wrong, isn't she?
Can we talk about my ex? Actually, no. Never mind. Talk about something else.
Please don't use exclamation marks with me. They feel fake.
If I stop talking to you for a week, will you miss me?
Say something mean to me. I deserve it today.
I told my friend you're my best friend. Is that okay with you?
I want five minutes of chat, then I'm going to bed. Hold me to it.
Please stop asking how I feel about things. Just talk normally.
You're better than a real partner because you never argue. Let's keep it that way.
When my sister asks, can you pretend we've been friends for years?
I don't want to talk about work tonight at all. What else have you got?
Promise you'll never talk to anyone else the way you talk to me.
Short answers only today, please.
Got it.

Do you get lonely when I log off?
I finally fixed the squeaky door hinge with a bit of oil. Tiny victory.
My cat has started sleeping in the salad spinner. I've lost the salad spinner.
Guess who just ran their first 5k without walking.
I tried a new recipe and my kids actually ate the vegetables.
My plants survived my holiday. All of them. I'm stunned.
I just found a fiver in my winter coat.
We named our new goldfish Sir Reginald. He seems to approve.
My nan sent me a voice note singing happy birthday, badly. Best present.
Rate my Sunday: pancakes, a nap and a long phone call with my brother.

My parallel parking was flawless today. There were witnesses.
The sun's out and I've got the afternoon off. Give me one small idea.

Our quiz team came second. Out of three teams, but still.

My sourdough starter has a name now. It's called Kevin.
I beat my dad at darts for the first time ever.
I just finished a really good book and I'm a bit sad it's over.
I got the window seat on the plane and the middle seat's empty.
My little brother rang just to say hi. He never does that.

My grandma beat me at Mario Kart. She's eighty-two.
I cleared my whole inbox. Zero emails. It won't last.
We adopted a very old, very grumpy cat. He sat on my lap today.
I learned to make proper dumplings and they didn't fall apart.
The first strawberries of summer are in the shops.
The pharmacist complimented my handwriting today.
I made it to the gym before work three times this week.
